Colitis ulcerosa (ulcerative colitis) is one of the two primary forms of [[inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Inflammatoriske tarmsygdomme]] (inflammatory bowel disease), alongside [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] [^src5]. In Denmark, the condition is systematically tracked and evaluated by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD), the national quality database for [[ibd|IBD]]. To be included in the registry, patients must have at least two hospital contacts registered in the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] with specific action diagnoses, including the DK51* code for ulcerative colitis [^src6]. The database also monitors related conditions and complications within the IBD spectrum, such as [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] and [[korttarmssyndrom|korttarmssyndrom]] [^src6].

As the second primary IBD diagnosis in the national reports, colitis ulcerosa represents a highly significant portion of the patient population, underscoring its clinical relevance in DANIBD's indicator system. Epidemiological data from the 2023 reporting period (October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023) shows that 58% of newly diagnosed adults were identified with colitis ulcerosa [^src2]. This substantial prevalence continued into the 2024 reporting period (October 1, 2023, to September 30, 2024). During this later period, 751 children and youth with IBD were in contact with a hospital department, 27% of whom were newly diagnosed [^src4]. Furthermore, registry data indicates that 7% of the broader IBD cohort were newly diagnosed, with the majority of these new cases (58%) being colitis ulcerosa, and half of the patients diagnosed before the age of 40 (median age: 39) [^src4].

## Claims
**Epidemiological**
- 58 % af de nydiagnosticerede voksne har colitis ulcerosa [^src1]
- I denne årsrapportperiode fra 1. oktober 2023 til og med 30. september 2024 har 751 børn og unge med IBD været i kontakt med en hospitalsafdeling, hvoraf 27 % af børnene er nydiagnosticerede med IBD i perioden [^src1]
- Heraf er 7 % nydiagnosticerede med IBD, hvoraf flest blev diagnosticeret med colitis ulcerosa (58 %) og halvdelen blev diagnosticeret før de fyldte 40 år (median: 39 år) [^src1]

**Eligibility-criteria**
- DANIBD omfatter alle patienter med IBD i Danmark, der har mindst to hospitalskontakter med aktionsdiagnoser DK50*, DK51*, DK830F eller DK912B i Landspatientregisteret [^src1]
